inherited.problem: 「门客里有一位侯嬴」把侯嬴的身份提前了：证据中他当时是魏国隐士、大梁夷门监者（E4），是无忌去请的人，直到宴罢才「侯生遂為上客」（E38），并非门客之一。
inherited.suggestion: 改为「魏国有位隐士侯嬴，年七十，家贫，在大梁夷门守门」，「宴罢，侯嬴成为上客」保留。

inherited.problem: 说侯嬴自刭的动机「没有更多交代」与证据矛盾：E20有侯生自述动机「北鄉自剄，以送公子」。
inherited.suggestion: 改为「侯嬴自刭除自述『以送公子』外再无交代；如姬盗符之后的下落，原文没有记载」。

inherited.problem: [unsupported_claims] 「话也越说越重」：证据只载平原君使者一次责让之辞，无多次递进的记载
[unsupported_claims] 「赵王因他一再辞让」中的「一再」
[unsupported_claims] 「门客里有一位侯嬴」：当时他尚非门客，是夷门监者、魏国隐士
[unsupported_claims] 「侯嬴自刭的动机……原文只写行为和一句话，没有更多交代」：E20载有其自述动机「以送公子」
[unsupported_claims] 「后来赵王以主人之礼相迎」：很可能是E23同一场迎接，非另一次
[quote_mismatches] 「诸侯之所以敬重他，『徒以有魏也』」：原文为「公子所以重於趙，名聞諸侯者，徒以有魏也」，主体与含义被缩改
[quote_mismatches] 「始吾聞平原君賢，故負魏王而救趙」为节引，脱「以稱平原君」，译文把动机改为「以为平原君贤明」

The Chinese labels this as the author's own inference (「作者推断」), but the English opens with "One reading:", which turns an attributed judgment into an anonymous possible reading and also makes the sentence read as if the reading itself is the mistake.
inherited.suggestion: Restore the attribution: "The author's inference: treating this as a friend staking everything for a friend would miss where the real difficulty lay."

inherited.problem: The English adds many facts that are not in the Chinese: Master Mao living among gamblers and Master Xue among ale-sellers, the king of Wei meeting Wuji in tears and giving him the seal of supreme commander, the rout "beyond the river", the general Meng Ao, the pursuit to the Hangu Pass, "ten thousand jin of gold", the content of the slander (exile ten years / they want to make him king) and that the king heard it daily, "set up its first commandery there", and "put Daliang to the sword"; the Chinese only has 重金, 破秦, 拔二十城, 俘虏了魏王.
inherited.suggestion: Trim these additions from the English (keep "much gold", "routed Qin", "took twenty cities", "captured the king of Wei"), or add the same details to the Chinese.

contamination.brief_line: 方向：这篇讲魏安釐王二十年邯郸被围、魏王不敢出兵时，信陵君决定偷虎符、杀本国将军晋鄙、夺军救赵（SJ0771-E9）（SJ0771-E10）（SJ0771-E12）。看点有三处：他出发送死前先折返问侯生，被当面点破是“以肉投餒虎”的盲动（SJ0771-E13）（SJ0771-E14）；动手前先为“晋鄙不交兵权”这个坏情况备好人手（SJ0771-E17）（SJ0771-E18）；事成之后不居功，听门客提醒后立即自责（SJ0771-E24）。不要写成“为朋友两肋插刀”的义气赞美，也不要写成窃符杀将的道德审判，要看他在没有干净选项时怎么准备、怎么付代价、怎么面对自己这方的亏欠。
- 秦王派使者告魏王：邯郸旦暮且下，敢救者移兵先击之；魏王惧，使人止晋鄙，留军壁邺，名为救赵，实持两端以观望（SJ0771-E10）。
- 公子数请魏王，宾客辩士说王万端，魏王畏秦终不听；公子自度不能得之于王，约车骑百余乘，欲以客往赴秦军，与赵俱死（SJ0771-E12）。
- 公子从其计，如姬果然盗出晋鄙兵符给公子（SJ0771-E16）。
- 公子到邺矫魏王令代晋鄙；晋鄙合符后起疑，说今拥十万之众屯于境上、国之重任，单车来代是怎么回事，欲无听（SJ0771-E21）。

必须写明的不确定性：本篇只有一个史源（《史记·魏公子列传》一处记述），其中的密语与对话（如侯嬴屏人间语献计、朱亥答话）是史家记述，未必逐字（SJ0771-E15）（SJ0771-E19）；不要替人物写心理，原文的“心不快”“意骄矜”“立自责”只是叙述用语，不是实录（SJ0771-E13）（SJ0771-E24）；不要换算公元年份，只用原文的魏安釐王二十年这样的纪年（SJ0771-E9）；“得选兵八万人”这一数字只此一处，无旁证（SJ0771-E22）；晋鄙军中如何收场、合符如何校验，原文没有记载（SJ0771-E21）（SJ0771-E22）；侯生自刭的动机、如姬盗符的后续，原文只写行为与一句话，没有更多交代（SJ0771-E20）（SJ0771-E16）。
现代应用：今天常见的情形是：你所在的团队遇到明显风险，但决策层因为害怕更大的对手而不肯动（SJ0771-E10）；你手里有一线证据和能干的人，要不要绕开常规流程推动（SJ0771-E12）；动手前先问一句“这是不是拿肉投餒虎”，并为“对方不配合”备好预案（SJ0771-E14）（SJ0771-E17）；事情成了之后不居功，主动承认对自己这方的亏欠（SJ0771-E24）。
注意：以下摘录的锚点未通过逐字核对，已删除，不得使用其内容：SJ0771-E10、SJ0771-E12、SJ0771-E16、SJ0771-E21。

issues.problem: 英文写 Hou Ying 是 "an old gatekeeper he trusted"。其中 "he trusted" 是证据外的关系和心理判断。中文此处完全没有交代侯嬴的身份，中英不一致。

evidence.quote: 魏有隱士曰侯嬴，年七十，家貧，為大梁夷門監者

issues.proposed: 英文删去 "he trusted"，改为 "Hou Ying, the aged gatekeeper there"。中文改为“停下来见在夷门守门的老人侯嬴”。
issues.rationale: 英文删去无据的 he trusted，改为 the aged gatekeeper there；中文同步补出“守门的老人”，中英一致。

issues.problem: 中文开头第一次出现侯嬴时没有任何身份。读者不知道无忌为什么要停车见这个人。

evidence.quote: 為大梁夷門監者

issues.proposed: 同 F1，补“在夷门守门的老人”这一身份即可，不加其他生平。
issues.rationale: 中文首次出场处补“守门的老人”这一身份，不加其他生平。

issues.problem: “他的姐姐就在城里”和 "his own sister was inside the walls" 断言她身在被围的邯郸城中。证据只说她是平原君夫人，没有写她当时的位置。

evidence.quote: 公子姊為趙惠文王弟平原君夫人

issues.proposed: 改为“而他的姐姐是赵国平原君的夫人”，英文改为 "and his own sister was Lord Pingyuan's wife"。
issues.rationale: 删去姐姐身在城中的断言，改为她是平原君的夫人，中英同步。

issues.problem: hook.1 已经讲过以下内容：晋鄙十万军被止在邺、无忌数请魏王、宾客说王、魏王畏秦不听、百余乘车骑。context.0、context.1、context.3 又逐项重讲一遍，“魏安釐王二十年”也在 hook.0 和 context.0 各出现一次。开头与背景重复同一套情节。

evidence.quote: 公子患之，數請魏王，及賓客辯士說王萬端

issues.proposed: hook.1 只保留处境与难处，删去其中数请魏王、宾客说王的细节，交给 context.3 叙述。context.0 删去重复的纪年。不新增内容。
issues.rationale: hook.1 删去数请魏王、宾客说王、魏王畏秦不听等细节，只保留处境，交由 context.3 叙述；context.0 删去重复的纪年。

issues.problem: “话也越说越重”和 "grew sharper with every trip" 写成了多次、逐步加重的责备。证据只记使者络绎不绝，以及一段责让之辞。

evidence.quote: 平原君使者冠蓋相屬於魏，讓魏公子曰

issues.proposed: 中文删去“话也越说越重”，改为“责备公子说”。英文删去 "and their reproaches grew sharper with every trip"。
issues.rationale: 删去“话也越说越重”及 grew sharper with every trip，改为一次责让，中英同步。

issues.problem: “门客里有一位侯嬴”和 "Among the retainers was Hou Ying" 把侯嬴写成了门客。证据中他当时是魏国隐士、夷门监者，宴罢才成为上客。

evidence.quote: 魏有隱士曰侯嬴
侯生遂為上客

issues.proposed: 中文改为“魏国有位隐士侯嬴”，英文改为 "Wei had a recluse named Hou Ying"。
issues.rationale: 把侯嬴的身份改为魏国隐士，宴罢才成为上客，中英同步。

issues.problem: 英文把“上客”译为 "chief retainer"，含有首席门客的职位意味，与中文“上客”（上宾）不等。

evidence.quote: 侯生遂為上客

issues.proposed: 改为 "Hou Ying became one of Wuji's most honored guests"。
issues.rationale: chief retainer 改为 one of Wuji's most honored guests，与“上客”对应。

issues.problem: 英文增写了兵符的形制和用法："matched half to half, one side held by the general, one by the king"。证据只说兵符藏在王的卧内，没有这一说明。

evidence.quote: 嬴聞晉鄙之兵符常在王臥內

issues.proposed: 删去这一插入语，改为 "Jin Pi's command tally was normally kept in the king of Wei's bedchamber"。
issues.rationale: 删去英文里兵符形制和用法的插入说明，只保留藏于王卧内。

issues.problem: “说出真正的办法”和 "the one plan that could work" 是作者的评价，却写成了事实，证据没有这样的判断。
issues.proposed: 中文改为“侯嬴献上一个计策”，英文改为 "Hou Ying laid out a plan"。
issues.rationale: “真正的办法”和 the one plan that could work 改为中性的“献上一个计策”和 laid out a plan。

issues.problem: “侯嬴则说自己年老不能随行”和 "said he was too old to go" 被放进了 E20 这次献计。证据里“老臣不能從”是此前夷门辞别时说的话，E20 只记他请求计算行期、自刭相送。

evidence.quote: 老臣不能從
請數公子行日，以至晉鄙軍之日，北鄉自剄，以送公子

issues.proposed: 删去“说自己年老不能随行”，直接写“侯嬴则请求算着无忌的行程……”。英文同步删去。
issues.rationale: 删去错置在此次献计中的“年老不能随行”，只写请求计算行期、自刭相送，中英同步。

issues.problem: “一再辞让”和 "kept declining" 夸大了次数。证据只说因为公子退让。

evidence.quote: 以公子退讓也

issues.proposed: 中文改为“赵王因他退让”，英文改为 "Because Wuji held back"。
issues.rationale: “一再辞让”和 kept declining 改为“退让”和 held back。

issues.problem: 英文把门客说的“矯魏王令”译为 "on your own authority"，丢掉了“假传魏王命令”的意思。中文是“矫魏王令”，中英不一致。

evidence.quote: 且矯魏王令，奪晉鄙兵以救趙

issues.proposed: 改为 "Forging the king of Wei's order and seizing Jin Pi's army"。
issues.rationale: 英文改为 Forging the king of Wei's order，恢复“矫魏王令”的意思。

issues.problem: 引语截去了“以稱平原君”。白话把“聞”译成“以为”，英文又加了无据的 "years later"。“回顾此事”也掩盖了这句话的场合：公子因平原君讥他结交博徒、卖浆者，辞别平原君夫人时说了这句话。

evidence.quote: 公子乃謝夫人去
故負魏王而救趙，以稱平原君

issues.proposed: 中文改为：后来他因平原君轻视他结交的人，要离开时说「始吾聞平原君賢，故負魏王而救趙，以稱平原君」——当初听说平原君贤明，才辜负魏王去救赵，好配得上平原君。英文删去 "years later"，补出 "to live up to Lord Pingyuan" 和说话的场合。
issues.rationale: 补全引语中的“以稱平原君”，把“聞”译为“听说”。交代说话场合：平原君讥笑他与赌徒、卖浆者交游，他辞别姐姐（平原君夫人）要离开。英文删去 years later，改为不加引号的译述。

issues.problem: “无忌的第一步不是去拼命，而是折回夷门，问侯嬴有没有别的做法”与证据不符。他已经上路赴死，折回是因为侯嬴没有送他一言半辞而心中不快，所以回来问自己有什么过失。侯嬴自己也这样解释他折返的原因。

evidence.quote: 我豈有所失哉？復引車還，問侯生
公子遇臣厚，公子往而臣不送，以是知公子恨之復返也

issues.proposed: 改为“无忌折回夷门，本是问侯嬴自己有何过失；侯嬴却借这次折返点破赴死无益”。英文同步修改。
issues.rationale: 改为：无忌折回是来问侯嬴自己有何过失，侯嬴借这次折返点破赴死无益。英文同步修改，并把古文引语改为不加引号的译述。

issues.problem: “动手之前他已经知道……兵符再真，晋鄙也可能不交兵权”和“给坏情况留人手”把预判与安排人手归给了无忌。证据中提醒风险、推荐朱亥的是侯嬴，无忌只是听从并流泪。

evidence.quote: 臣客屠者朱亥可與俱，此人力士

issues.proposed: 改为“侯嬴提醒他兵符合上晋鄙也可能不交兵权，并让他带上朱亥；无忌听后预见要杀本国老将，先流泪说破”。英文同步修改。
issues.rationale: 把预判风险、安排朱亥同行归还给侯嬴；无忌只是听后预见要杀老将并流泪。中英同步。

issues.problem: 正文夹有证据编号括注，如（SJ0771-E17）。analysis.2、analysis.3、analysis.4、limits.0、limits.1、limits.2 也有。这属于审核过程，不应出现在正文里。
issues.proposed: 删去所有正文中的证据编号括注。
issues.rationale: 删去 analysis.1–4 和 limits.0–2 正文中所有证据编号括注，编号只保留在 ev 中。

issues.problem: “只递证据、不动自己的位置”把现代应用的框架带进了历史分析：无忌并没有可以“递上去的证据”。这一段也与 reflection.example.alternative 重复。按第 13 条，现代场景只放在开放问题里。
issues.proposed: 删去“作者设想的另一种做法：只递证据、不动自己的位置”一句，或改为“另一种做法是继续等魏王回心转意”。英文同步修改。
issues.rationale: 删去“只递证据、不动自己的位置”这一现代框架，改为“继续等魏王回心转意”，中英同步。

issues.problem: “诸侯之所以敬重他，「徒以有魏也」”改动了原句的主体和含义。原文说的是公子在赵国受重视、名闻诸侯，都只因为背后有魏国。

evidence.quote: 公子所以重於趙，名聞諸侯者，徒以有魏也

issues.proposed: 改为“毛公、薛公说，公子在赵国受重视、名闻诸侯，「徒以有魏也」——只因背后有魏国”。
issues.rationale: 改为毛公、薛公说公子在赵国受重视、名闻诸侯，只因背后有魏国，与原句的主体一致。

issues.problem: “褒扬落在他敬重侯嬴这一端，而不在矫令杀将上”是作者的推断，没有标注。太史公原话说的是结交岩穴隐者，没有点名侯嬴。

evidence.quote: 然信陵君之接岩穴隱者，不恥下交，有以也

issues.proposed: 前面加“作者认为”，英文加 "One reading is that"。
issues.rationale: 褒扬落点一句中文标“作者认为”，英文标 One reading is that；措辞改为“侯嬴这类隐士”，不说太史公点了侯嬴的名。

issues.problem: 全文一直称“无忌/Wuji”，这里突然改称“信陵君/Xinling”，读者会以为是另一个人。中文里的毛公、薛公也是首次出现，没有交代身份（英文交代了）。

evidence.quote: 公子聞趙有處士毛公藏於博徒，薛公藏於賣漿家

issues.proposed: 写作“太史公称无忌为信陵君”，此后仍用无忌。中文补“他在赵国结交的隐士毛公、薛公”。
issues.rationale: 写明太史公称无忌为信陵君，此后仍称无忌；中文补出毛公、薛公是他在赵国结交的隐士。

issues.problem: 英文比中文多出大量事实：毛公、薛公的出身，魏王相泣并授上将军印，河外、蒙骜、函谷关，金万斤，毁谤的具体内容，魏王日闻其毁，初置东郡，屠大梁。这些在证据中有据，但中文缺失，中英不一致。

evidence.quote: 秦王患之，乃行金萬斤於魏，求晉鄙客
拔二十城，初置東郡

issues.proposed: 按第 15 条，压缩英文，只保留与中文对应的要点：归魏为将、率五国破秦、秦用重金收买晋鄙门客毁谤、被代将、四年后病酒而死、秦拔二十城、十八年后俘魏王。
issues.rationale: 压缩英文，只保留与中文对应的要点：归魏为将、率五国破秦、重金收买晋鄙门客毁谤、被代将、四年后病酒而死、秦拔二十城、十八年后俘魏王。

issues.problem: “没有第二种记载可以对勘”和 "with no second version to check it against" 是对完整来源与其他文献的断言，证据包无法支持。这一说法来自已知污染 K6 的简报。
issues.proposed: 改为“本文只依据《史记·魏公子列传》”，删去“没有第二种记载可以对勘”。
issues.rationale: 删去“没有第二种记载可以对勘”，改为本文只依据本传，中英同步。

issues.problem: 说侯嬴自刭的动机“没有更多交代”，与证据矛盾。侯嬴自己说明了自刭是为了送公子。

evidence.quote: 北鄉自剄，以送公子

issues.proposed: 删去关于侯嬴动机“没有交代”的半句。英文同步删去。
issues.rationale: 删去关于侯嬴自刭动机没有交代的半句，中英同步，ev 去掉 E20。

issues.problem: “如姬盗符之后的下落……没有更多交代”是对完整来源的“未载”断言，沿用了已知污染 K6（引自已剔除的 E16）。读者理解主线也不需要这一点。

evidence.quote: 如姬果盜晉鄙兵符與公子

issues.rationale: 删去关于如姬下落的“未载”断言，中英同步，ev 去掉 E28。

edits.before: 门客里有一位侯嬴，年七十，家贫，在大梁夷门守门。无忌想厚赠他，他不肯收，说自己修身絜行几十年，终不能因为守门穷困而受财。无忌于是置酒大会宾客，空出车上左边的尊位，亲自去迎侯嬴。侯嬴穿着破旧衣冠，径直登上上座，也不谦让，为的是看无忌的反应；无忌执辔，愈恭。侯嬴又在集市上故意站了很久，让过路人都来围观；无忌的脸色始终不变。到家后无忌请他坐上座，向在座宾客一一介绍，宾客皆惊。侯嬴后来自己说破：他这样做是想成全公子礼贤下士的名声；市人因此把他看作小人，称无忌是能下士的长者。宴罢，侯嬴成为上客。

edits.before: Among the retainers was Hou Ying, seventy years old and poor, a gatekeeper at the Yimen. Wuji sought him out and tried to present him with a handsome gift. Hou Ying would not take it: he had kept himself and his conduct clean for decades, he said, and would not accept the prince's money simply because gatekeeping left him poor. So Wuji laid on a feast for all his retainers, and once the guests were seated, he went out with his carriage and escort, left the seat of honor on the left of the chariot empty, and fetched Hou Ying himself. Hou Ying, in his shabby robe and cap, climbed straight up into that seat without a word of demur — a test of Wuji, this was — and Wuji took the reins and grew only more respectful. Hou Ying then stood about a long time in the marketplace so that passers-by would stare; Wuji's manner never changed. At the house Wuji showed Hou Ying to the seat of honor and presented him to the assembled guests one by one, and the guests were astonished. Hou Ying later spelled out his reasoning: he was a mere gatekeeper, and the prince had personally come for him before a crowd. "I wanted to make your name," he said, "so I stood a long time by your carriage in the market while people watched, and the more I tried you, the more respectful you became. The townsfolk took me for a lout and you for a true elder who can humble himself before scholars." When the feast broke up, Hou Ying became Wuji's chief retainer.

edits.before: 折回夷门之后，侯嬴说出真正的办法。晋鄙的兵符平时收在魏王卧室内；如姬最得魏王宠爱，出入卧内，有能力偷出来。侯嬴说，如姬的父亲被人所杀，她为此出资三年，从魏王以下都想替她报父仇而未能；如姬向无忌哭诉，无忌派门客斩了仇人的头献给她。侯嬴的判断是：如姬愿为公子死，只是没有机会；公子一开口，她必答应。得虎符，夺晋鄙军，北救赵而西却秦，「此五霸之伐也」。

edits.before: Back at the Yimen, Hou Ying laid out the one plan that could work. The command tally that authenticated orders to Jin Pi's army — matched half to half, one side held by the general, one by the king — was normally kept in the king of Wei's bedchamber. Lady Ru, the king's favorite, came and went in the bedchamber freely and could steal it out. Hou Ying spelled out why she would. Her father had been murdered; for three years she had put up money to see her father's death avenged, and no one, the king included, had been able to bring it off. She had wept to Wuji, who sent a retainer to cut off her enemy's head and present it to her. Hou Ying's judgment was that Lady Ru would gladly die for Wuji and had simply never had the chance to serve him; one word from the prince and she would agree. Get the tally, take over Jin Pi's army, go north to rescue Zhao and push Qin back from the west — "an achievement worthy of the Five Hegemons."

edits.before: This time Zhu Hai answered without hesitation: "I am a knife-wielding butcher in the market. You have come to see me in person again and again, and I never answered in kind because small courtesies are of no use. Now that you are in a fix, this is the moment for me to give my life." edits.before: 赵孝成王感激他矫令夺兵而存赵，与平原君商量，要拿五座城封给他。无忌听说，「意驕矜而有自功之色」。一位门客劝他：别人对你有德，不可忘；你对别人有德，最好忘掉。矫魏王令、夺晋鄙兵，「於趙則有功矣，於魏則未為忠臣也」，还自骄自功，我私下以为不可取。无忌「立自責，似若無所容者」。后来赵王以主人之礼相迎，无忌侧身辞让，自言有罪过，「以負於魏，無功於趙」。赵王因他一再辞让，口不忍献五城，最后把鄗给他作汤沐邑，魏国也把信陵还给他。

edits.before: King Xiaocheng of Zhao, grateful that Wuji had seized the army on a forged order and saved Zhao, took counsel with Lord Pingyuan and proposed to enfeoff him with five cities. When Wuji heard, he "showed a self-satisfied look, as if the credit were his own." A retainer came to him: kindness done to you must never be forgotten, he said; kindness you do to another is best forgotten. Taking the tally and Jin Pi's army on your own authority — "toward Zhao you have done a service; toward Wei you cannot be called a loyal minister." To go on preening yourself over it is something I cannot approve. Wuji "at once blamed himself, as if there were nowhere he could hide." Later, when the king of Zhao received him with the rites of a host, Wuji stood to the side, declined the honor, and pronounced himself at fault: "I have failed Wei and done nothing for Zhao." Because he kept declining, the king of Zhao could not bring himself to hand over the five cities. In the end the king gave him the town of Hao to support his household, and Wei restored to him the city of Xinling.

edits.before: One reading: treat this as a friend staking everything for a friend and you miss where the real difficulty lay. Wuji's first move was not to charge but to turn back at the Yimen. His question to Hou Ying was whether there was another way. Hou Ying's rebuke — "it would be like throwing meat at a starving tiger. What would it accomplish? And what use would your retainers be then?" — traded courage for arithmetic: what would a hundred-odd chariots buy against the Qin army? If even his retainers could not be put to use, what were retainers for?
edits.after: The author's inference: treat this as a friend staking everything for a friend and you miss where the real difficulty lay. Wuji turned back at the Yimen to ask Hou Ying what fault he had committed; Hou Ying used that return to show him that riding to his death would accomplish nothing. His rebuke — it would be like throwing meat at a starving tiger; what would it accomplish, and what use would retainers be then? — traded courage for arithmetic: what would a hundred-odd chariots buy against the Qin army? If even his retainers could not be put to use, what were retainers for?

edits.before: What did Sima Qian make of it? The Grand Historian writes that he passed through Daliang and made a point of finding the Yimen, and adds that Xinling's readiness to seek out recluses in mountain caves and to befriend men beneath him was something he had real cause for: "his name stood first among the lords — no empty fame." The praise lands on the end where he honored Hou Ying, not on the forged order and the slain general. And the costs did not stop there. Wuji stayed in Zhao ten years. When Qin attacked Wei, the two recluses he had befriended there — Master Mao, who lived among gamblers, and Master Xue, who hid himself among ale-sellers — told him that the only reason he was respected in Zhao and known to the lords was that he had Wei behind him; he changed countenance at once, ordered the carriage, and went back to save Wei. The king of Wei met him in tears and gave him the seal of supreme commander. Wuji called the other states to arms, led their five armies to rout Qin beyond the river, put the general Meng Ao to flight, and pursued to the Hangu Pass, after which the Qin army dared not come out. Alarmed, the king of Qin sent ten thousand jin of gold into Wei to buy off Jin Pi's former retainers, who slandered Wuji to the king: he has been an exile ten years, the lords obey only him, they want to make him king. The king heard it daily and came to believe it; he sent a replacement to take over the army. Wuji, knowing he had been pushed aside by slander a second time, excused himself on illness and spent long nights drinking with his retainers, strong wine and women, for four years, until drink killed him. After his death Qin attacked Wei, took twenty cities and set up its first commandery there, and eighteen years later captured the king of Wei and put Daliang to the sword. One reading is that this closing episode writes Wuji's survival and Wei's survival on the same line.

edits.before: Wei had a recluse named Hou Ying, seventy years old and poor, a gatekeeper at the Yimen. Wuji sought him out and tried to present him with a handsome gift. Hou Ying would not take it: he had kept himself and his conduct clean for decades, he said, and would not accept the prince's money simply because gatekeeping left him poor. So Wuji laid on a feast for all his retainers, and once the guests were seated, he went out with his carriage and escort, left the seat of honor on the left of the chariot empty, and fetched Hou Ying himself. Hou Ying, in his shabby robe and cap, climbed straight up into that seat without a word of demur — a test of Wuji, this was — and Wuji took the reins and grew only more respectful. Hou Ying then stood about a long time in the marketplace so that passers-by would stare; Wuji's manner never changed. At the house Wuji showed Hou Ying to the seat of honor and presented him to the assembled guests one by one, and the guests were astonished. Hou Ying later spelled out his reasoning: he was a mere gatekeeper, and the prince had personally come for him before a crowd. "I wanted to make your name," he said, "so I stood a long time by your carriage in the market while people watched, and the more I tried you, the more respectful you became. The townsfolk took me for a lout and you for a true elder who can humble himself before scholars." When the feast broke up, Hou Ying became one of Wuji's most honored guests.
